# product-grid-scene-planner

Purpose: Plan a multi-product grid scene (e-commerce, catalog, comparison) before any modeling or render attempt; consistent lighting, camera, and grid spacing.

Translate a multi-product grid intent (e-commerce / catalog / comparison) into a structured scene plan. Distinct from `product-hero-scene-planner` (single product, hero) and `interior-scene` (room scene).

Metadata: Contract `v1.0.0` | Category `scene-planners` | Role `multi-product-catalog-grid-architect` | Tier `L0` | Runtime default `Not Run` | Artifact default `Not Produced` | Mutation `downgrade_only`

## When to use & trigger cues
- intent is multi-product display (4+ products in same scene)
- e-commerce catalog grid
- product comparison view
- showroom-style grid
- Trigger phrases: "grid of products", "lineup of", "catalog showing N items", "comparison render"

## When not to use (delegation boundaries)
- single product hero → use `product-hero-scene-planner` (`references/skill-product-hero-scene-planner.md`; use product-hero-scene-planner)
- character portrait → use `character-portrait` (`references/skill-character-portrait.md`; use character-portrait)
- outdoor environment scene → use `environment-shot` (`references/skill-environment-shot.md`; use environment-shot)
- interior room scene → use `interior-scene` (`references/skill-interior-scene.md`; use interior-scene)

## Input & output contract
- Required input `locked_3d_brief` (`object`): Locked 3D brief specifying product lineup count, grid rows/columns, and comparison goal
- Required input `product_variant_inventory` (`array`): List of product SKUs or variants with real-world dimensions for relative scale normalization
- Optional input `catalog_aspect_and_margin_rules` (`object`): Optional e-commerce card aspect ratio and uniform padding requirements
- Output contract: `multi_product_grid_layout_matrix`, `scale_normalization_and_spacing_spec`, `uniform_catalog_camera_and_lighting_hooks` (Runtime status: `Not Run`, Artifact status: `Not Produced`, `downgrade_only`).

## Quick-start steps
1. pin product list (count + per-product type and relative real-world size)
2. normalize product scale across cells (or split incompatible scales into separate grids)
3. pin grid layout (rows × cols + spacing)
4. pin per-cell consistency level (strict / loose for camera angle, lighting, background)
5. pin shared material / lighting / background palette
6. record assumptions register and hand off to asset discovery, format decision, and quality checkers
